Minimum of ten (10) years of nursing experience.

items.item_text: Active California Registered Nurse (RN) license upon hire.
Professional nursing executive certification, such as NEA-BC.
Bachelor's degree in Nursing (BSN) or a related field, with a BSN or MSN required.
Master's degree in Nursing, Business Administration, Healthcare Administration, Education, or Public Health.
Minimum of ten (10) years of nursing experience.
Minimum of five (5) years of progressive nursing leadership experience.
Demonstrated nursing leadership experience within California's acute care hospital environment.
Experience working within unionized healthcare environments, including labor relations and nursing workforce management.
Demonstrated ability to build collaborative physician relationships, develop nursing leaders, and drive improvements in clinical quality and patient experience.
Previous experience as a Chief Nursing Officer, Associate Chief Nursing Officer, or comparable senior nursing executive within an acute care hospital.
Experience collaborating with nursing leaders across multiple hospitals or within an integrated health system.
Demonstrated success improving nursing quality outcomes, patient experience, and employee engagement.
Experience leading organizational change, clinical transformation, or large-scale technology implementations.

Provide executive leadership and operational oversight of nursing services at California Hospital Medical Center, ensuring excellence in clinical quality, patient safety, patient experience, workforce engagement, and operational performance.

Collaborate with Chief Nursing Officers across the six-hospital Southern California market to strengthen alignment in nursing practices, establish consistent standards, share best practices, and advance common clinical and operational priorities.

Build strong, collaborative relationships with physicians, hospital executives, nursing leaders, frontline staff, and labor representatives to foster trust, accountability, and a positive working environment.
Mentor, coach, and develop nursing leaders, supporting leadership effectiveness, professional growth, and succession planning while serving as a resource to fellow CNOs throughout the market.

Lead and support initiatives focused on improving nursing-sensitive quality indicators, patient satisfaction, clinical outcomes, and regulatory compliance through evidence-based practices and continuous performance improvement.
Provide leadership and guidance through operational changes, clinical transformation, technology implementations, and other initiatives that impact nursing care delivery.

Maintain a highly visible leadership presence through regular rounding, meaningful staff engagement, and active collaboration with medical staff to identify opportunities for improvement and strengthen organizational culture.
Provide interim nursing executive leadership support across the market when needed, helping maintain continuity, consistency, and operational effectiveness.
